blocks.h2: Faucets and Fixtures in Evanston Homes
blocks.intro: Water and age both wear on fixtures.

items.body: Evanston's hard water leaves scale in aerators and cartridges.
We replace them during the job.
Older fixtures may need specific parts.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: Minerals in hard water build up where water sits and dries, like aerators, cartridges and spray heads. The first sign is often a spray that goes sideways or a weaker stream. Soaking the aerator in vinegar can help. When a single-handle faucet starts to drip or get stiff, the cartridge is usually worn by scale. Replacing it is a quick repair if parts are available for your model.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Faucet Work
blocks.body: Replacing a cartridge is quick. Replacing a faucet takes longer when the old one is stuck in place, when the sink is undermounted or when old shutoffs need to come out too. Vintage fixtures may need special parts. We look first and give you one flat price.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my faucet?
items.preview: If parts are available, repair is often cheaper.
items.answer: If it's a quality faucet with parts available, repair. If it's old and worn, replacement often makes more sense.

items.q: Can you install a faucet I bought?
items.answer: Yes, if it's complete and fits the sink.

items.q: Why is my faucet's flow weak?
items.answer: Usually mineral scale in the aerator or cartridge.
If they're stiff or original, yes.

items.q: Can you install a filtered-water faucet?
items.answer: Yes, along with the filter system under the sink.

items.q: Can you install a touchless faucet?
items.answer: Yes. Most need an outlet or batteries under the sink.

items.q: How much does faucet repair cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the faucet. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the faucet and what's wrong. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
